newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent slips further, Med/W Africa also weak.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent slips further, Med/W Africa also weak.

text.p: Benchmark Dated Brent saw its value slide again on Thursday under the weight of ample prompt North Sea supply and slack demand from refineries struggling with poor product margins, traders said.
A Brent cargo due to load March 20-22 was sold by a Wall Street trader to a European major for April Brent less 15 cents a barrel, seven cents weaker than on Wednesday.
The clocking to Statoil of the sole Brent nominated March 21-23 loading on Thursday confirmed the weak tone, traders said.
"The North Sea is looking pretty weak at the moment and there's no arbitrage -- it's not even close," said a trader.

While 600,000 barrels of Norwegian Ekofisk loading March 23-25 were heard traded in line with Tuesday's deal at Dated Brent +35 cents, a cargo loading three days earlier fetched only Dated Brent +29.50 cents.
April Brent gained 20 cents to $19.60 a barrel, helped by firmer U.S. products, but spreads and CFDs lost ground.
March/April lost four cents to trade at +8 while next week's CFDs were talked about 10 cents lower at May Brent +8 cents.
BP has become the latest ARA refiner to cut throughput due to the current margin squeeze, trimming runs by about 12 percent at its Nerefco complex, a 65-35 joint venture with Texaco.
Brent cracking margins in ARA are currently below $1 a barrel.
Mediterranean and West African trade remained in the doldrums, struggling with excess supply and reticent buyers.
Two traders offered Urals at a discount to Dated Brent in the 90s but most players said the market was still around the Dated -$1.05 cents done for a March 14-16 loader on Wednesday.

"The sour market in the Med is very, very quiet and Urals is a crapshoot," a trader said. "People are going to sit back and wait for those differentials to move further downwards. Refiners with bad margins are looking to buy at the bottom."
